text: After this you can recognize when a time-based cash-flow analysis is more useful than payback.

Project decisions may require more than a payback estimate. Net present value (NPV) brings later net cash flows into present-value terms before accounting for initial investment. Internal rate of return (IRR) is the discount rate at which NPV is zero. Life-cycle costing totals relevant costs over a defined period, while a savings-to-investment measure relates discounted benefits and expense. Vary uncertain inputs to see whether a result is robust. This is educational, not financial advice.

items: Inferred: Illustrative calculation: Spend $1,000 initially and receive $600 at each of the next two year-ends. At 10% discount, NPV = −1000 + 600/1.1 + 600/1.1² = approximately $41.32.

text: Use discounted cash flows for long-lived or uneven projects.
Simple payback alone omits future timing and many ownership costs.
